subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message sender identity contract for multi-agent conversations, and what exact metadata should be canonical across protocol, transcripts, events, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: The current code has several partial attribution mechanisms, but the requested fix changes public gateway and persisted session semantics, so automation should not choose the canonical identity shape.

options.title: Design additive sender metadata
options.body: Add a durable sender identity object with sender id, kind, display name, source session/agent, and renderable avatar/color metadata, then migrate UI and session surfaces to consume it.

options.title: Keep narrow partial fixes
options.body: Continue landing scoped senderLabel and sessions_send prompt fixes while leaving the broader durable identity contract unimplemented for now.

options.title: Defer multi-agent identity
options.body: Leave this open as a roadmap item until a larger multi-agent/session model design is prioritized.

recommendation.title: Design additive sender metadata
recommendation.body: Add a durable sender identity object with sender id, kind, display name, source session/agent, and renderable avatar/color metadata, then migrate UI and session surfaces to consume it.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans protocol, session provenance, transcript semantics, and product direction, and steipete has the strongest recent history on those central surfaces.
